offset 0x04 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
13:2GENCTRLnone per bitR0x0One bit per generator: set while GENCTRLn is synchronizing between clock domains, cleared when that or a clock switch is done.

GENCTRLnGenerator Controlp. 151

offset 0x20 · 12 copies, every 0x04 · 32 bits · reset 0b00000000000000000000000100000000 · access R/W · pac write-protection, write-synchronized

  • The register's reset value is also given as 0x00000106.
  • Controls generator n, n = 0 to 11.
  • After a power reset GENCTRL0 is 0x00000106 and the others 0x00000000. A user reset gives the same values, except a generator feeding a peripheral channel with PCHCTRLm.WRTLOCK=1 keeps its register.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:16DIVR/W0x0Division value for the generator, used as set by DIVSEL. Generators 0 and 2 to 11 use DIV[7:0] (largest factor 512); generator 1 uses DIV[15:0] (largest factor 131072). Bits written outside that range are ignored.
13RUNSTDBYR/W0Keeps the generator running in Standby while it drives its GCLK_IOn pin. With OE at 0 it has no effect, and the generator runs only when a peripheral needs the clock.
0Generator stops in Standby; GCLK_IOn sits at the level set by OOV.
1Generator keeps running and driving GCLK_IOn in Standby.
12DIVSELR/W0Selects how DIV becomes the division factor. To leave the source undivided, DIVSEL must be 0 and DIV must be 0 or 1.
0Source frequency divided by DIV.
1Source frequency divided by 2^(N+1), N being the generator's number of DIV bits.
11OER/W0Drives the generator clock out on its GCLK_IOn pin, unless that pin is the generator's SRC.
0No clock on GCLK_IOn.
1Clock on GCLK_IOn, unless GCLK_IOn is the source in SRC.
10OOVR/W0Level on GCLK_IOn while the generator is off or OE is 0, unless that pin is the generator's SRC.
0Low.
1High.
9IDCR/W0Balances the output duty cycle to 50/50 when the division factor is odd.
0Not balanced for odd factors.
150/50 duty cycle.
8GENENR/W1Turns the generator on or off.
0Off.
1On.
3:0SRCR/W0x0Selects the generator's clock source.
0x00XOSC0XOSC0 output.
0x01XOSC1XOSC1 output.
0x02GCLK_INGCLK_IO input pad.
0x03GCLK_GEN1Generator 1 output.
0x04OSCULP32KOSCULP32K output.
0x05XOSC32KXOSC32K output.
0x06DFLLDFLL48M output.
0x07DPLL0FDPLL200M 0 output.
0x08DPLL1FDPLL200M 1 output.
0x09-0x0FReservedReserved.

PCHCTRLmPeripheral Channel Controlp. 154

offset 0x80 · 48 copies, every 0x04 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W · pac write-protection

  • Controls peripheral channel m, m = 0 to 47.
  • Channel map: 0 DFLL48 input; 1 FDPLL0 reference; 2 FDPLL1 reference; 3 FDPLL0 and FDPLL1 32 kHz lock timer clocks, SDHC0 and SDHC1 slow, SERCOM0 to 7 slow; 4 EIC; 5 FREQM measure; 6 FREQM reference; 7 SERCOM0 core; 8 SERCOM1 core; 9 TC0, TC1; 10 USB; 11 to 22 EVSYS0 to 11; 23 SERCOM2 core; 24 SERCOM3 core; 25 TCC0, TCC1; 26 TC2, TC3; 27 CAN0; 28 CAN1; 29 TCC2, TCC3; 30 TC4, TC5; 31 PDEC; 32 AC; 33 CCL; 34 SERCOM4 core; 35 SERCOM5 core; 36 SERCOM6 core; 37 SERCOM7 core; 38 TCC4; 39 TC6, TC7; 40 ADC0; 41 ADC1; 42 DAC; 43 to 44 I2S; 45 SDHC0; 46 SDHC1; 47 CM4 trace.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7WRTLOCKR/W0Once set to 1, later writes to PCHCTRLm are dropped and the GENCTRLn chosen by GEN is locked too; only a power reset unlocks them. Generator 0 cannot be locked.
0Not locked.
1Channel and its generator locked.
6CHENR/W0Turns the peripheral channel on or off.
0Off.
1On.
3:0GENR/W0x0Picks the generator that clocks the peripheral channel. A power reset clears GEN, CHEN and WRTLOCK to 0; a user reset clears them when WRTLOCK is 0 and leaves the register as it is when WRTLOCK is 1.
0x0Generator 0.
0x1Generator 1.
0x2Generator 2.
0x3Generator 3.
0x4Generator 4.
0x5Generator 5.
0x6Generator 6.
0x7Generator 7.
0x8Generator 8.
0x9Generator 9.
0xAGenerator 10.
0xBGenerator 11.

CLEARClearp. 262

offset 0x0C · 8 bits · reset 0x00 · access W · write-synchronized

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
7:0CLEARW0x0Key register that restarts the watchdog. Normal mode: writing 0xA5 inside the time-out period clears the timer and starts the period again. Window mode: any write during the closed window (TOWDTW) resets the system at once, and 0xA5 written during the open window (TOWDT) clears the timer and restarts the full closed-then-open sequence. In either mode, any value other than 0xA5 resets the system at once.

NCRGMAC Network Control Registerp. 483

offset 0x000 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
19LPIR/W0Set to 1 to turn on low power idle (LPI) transmission, sent at once on txd and tx_er.
18FNPR/W0Set to 1 to drop the next packet held in the external RX DPRAM; it acts only when the DMA is not already copying a stored packet from the DPRAM to memory.
17TXPBPFR/W0Sends a PFC priority-based pause frame built from the values held in TPFCP.
16ENPBPRR/W0Set to 1 to turn on reception of PFC priority-based pause frames: PFC negotiation and recognition of such frames.
0Normal operation.
1PFC priority-based pause frames are recognised.
15SRTSMR/W0Set to 1 to overwrite the CRC of each received frame with the nanoseconds field of the 1588 timer, as captured when the frame passed the message time stamp point.
0Normal operation.
1Every received frame's CRC holds a time stamp instead.
12TXZQPFR/W0Write 1 to send a pause frame with a zero quantum; writing 0 does nothing.
11TXPFR/W0Write 1 to send a pause frame; writing 0 does nothing.
10THALTR/W0Write 1 to stop transmitting once the frame in progress, if any, has gone out; writing 0 does nothing.
9TSTARTR/W0Write 1 to begin transmitting; writing 0 does nothing.
8BPR/W0At 1, in 10M or 100M half duplex, a collision is forced on every received frame; gigabit half duplex ignores it.
0No forced collisions.
1Collisions forced in 10M and 100M half duplex.
7WESTATR/W0Set to 1 so the statistics registers can be written, for functional test.
0Statistics registers cannot be written.
1Statistics registers can be written.
6INCSTATR/W0Write 1 to add one to every statistics register, for test; writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.
5CLRSTATR/W0Write 1 to zero the statistics registers; writing 0 does nothing. Always reads 0.
4MPER/W01 turns the management port on. 0 turns it off, puts MDIO in high impedance and drives MDC low impedance.
0Management port off.
1Management port on.
3TXENR/W01 lets the GMAC transmitter send data. 0 halts transmission at once, clears the transmit pipeline and control registers, and resets the transmit queue pointer to the first transmit descriptor.
0Transmitter off.
1Transmitter on.
2RXENR/W01 lets the GMAC receive data. 0 halts reception at once and clears the receive pipeline; the receive queue pointer is left as it is.
0Receiver off.
1Receiver on.
1LBLR/W01 ties GTX to GRX and GTXEN to GRXDV and forces full duplex. GRXCK and GTXCK may misbehave while switching into or out of internal loop back; receive and transmit must already be disabled before switching.
0Local loop back off.
1Local loop back on.

NCFGRGMAC Network Configuration Registerp. 486

offset 0x004 · 32 bits · reset 0x00080000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
30IRXERR/W0At 1, GRXER has no effect on the GMAC while GRXDV is low.
29RXBPR/W0At 1, frames whose preamble is non-standard are kept rather than rejected.
28IPGSENR/W0At 1, the transmit IPG may grow beyond 96 bit times according to the previous frame's length and IPGS.
26IRXFCSR/W0Keep at 0 for normal operation. At 1, frames with FCS/CRC errors are kept; bad-FCS statistics are still counted and the FCS status still goes into the frame's DMA descriptor.
25EFRHDR/W0At 1, frames can be received in half duplex while transmitting.
24RXCOENR/W0At 1, the receive checksum engine runs and frames with a bad IP, TCP or UDP checksum are dropped.
23DCPFR/W0At 1, valid pause frames are not copied to memory, whatever CAF, a hash match or a type ID match says; a destination address match still copies one. Valid pause frames still count in the pause statistics and still pause transmission.
22:21DBWR/W0x0Width of the data bus; 64 bits by default.
0DBW3232-bit bus.
1DBW6464-bit bus.
20:18CLKR/W0x2Divider from MCK to the management data clock MDC; set it to suit MCK so that MDC stays at or below 2.5 MHz for 802.3 conformance. MDC runs only during MDIO reads and writes.
0MCK_8MCK/8, MCK up to 20 MHz.
1MCK_16MCK/16, MCK up to 40 MHz.
2MCK_32MCK/32, MCK up to 80 MHz.
3MCK_48MCK/48, MCK up to 120 MHz.
4MCK_64MCK/64, MCK up to 160 MHz.
5MCK_96MCK/96, MCK up to 240 MHz.
17RFCSR/W0At 1, received frames go to memory without their 4-byte frame check sequence, and the reported length is 4 bytes shorter.
16LFERDR/W0At 1, a frame is dropped when its measured length is less than its length field (bytes 13 and 14 of an untagged frame); applies only to length fields below 0x0600.
15:14RXBUFOR/W0x0How many bytes into the receive buffer the received data starts.
13PENR/W0At 1, transmission pauses on receipt of a non-zero 802.3 classic pause frame, if PFC has not been negotiated.
12RTYR/W0Keep at 0 for normal operation. At 1, back-off between collisions is always one slot time, for testing the too-many-retries condition; it also shortens the pause counter's decrement from every 512 bit times to every GRXCK cycle, for pause frame tests.
8MAXFSR/W0At 1, frames up to 1536 bytes are accepted; at 0, any frame longer than 1518 bytes is rejected.
7UNIHENR/W01 accepts a unicast frame when the 6-bit hash of its destination address selects a set bit in the hash register; 0 turns unicast hashing off.
6MTIHENR/W01 accepts a multicast frame when the 6-bit hash of its destination address selects a set bit in the hash register; 0 turns multicast hashing off.
5NBCR/W01 rejects frames sent to the broadcast address 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF; 0 accepts them.
4CAFR/W0At 1, every valid frame is accepted.
3JFRAMER/W0At 1, jumbo frames up to 10240 bytes are accepted; 10240 bytes is the default length.
2DNVLANR/W01 passes only VLAN-tagged frames on to address matching; 0 passes tagged and untagged frames.
1FDR/W01 selects full duplex: the transmitter ignores collision and carrier sense, and reception can run during transmission. 0 turns full duplex off.
0SPDR/W01 selects 100 Mbps; 0 selects 10 Mbps.

TSRGMAC Transmit Status Registerp. 493

offset 0x014 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
8HRESPR/W0Set when the DMA receives an HRESP not OK. Write 1 to clear.
6UNDR/W0Set when the transmitter had to cut a frame short because no more data came, or when a transmit status write back was attempted before the previous one finished. With the DMA in internal FIFO mode it is also set when, after the SOP data went into the FIFO, the AHB grant came too late, an AHB not OK came back, or a used bit was read. Write 1 to clear.
5TXCOMPR/W0Set when a frame has gone out. Write 1 to clear.

3TXGOR/W0Reads 1 while transmission is active; with the DMA interface it is the TXGO variable of the transmit buffer description.
2RLER/W0Retry limit exceeded flag. Write 1 to clear.
1COLR/W0In 10/100 Mbps mode, set by a collision or a late collision. Write 1 to clear.
0UBRR/W0Set when the DMA reads a transmit buffer descriptor whose used bit is 1. Write 1 to clear.

RBQBGMAC Receive Buffer Queue Base Address Registerp. 495

offset 0x018 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W · read/write

  • Where the list of receive buffer descriptors begins. Write it before NCR.RXEN turns reception on; once reception is on, writes are ignored. A read gives the address of the descriptor now in use, which moves on as buffers fill, so received frames are found by walking the descriptor list and checking each used bit, not by reading this register. Descriptors sit on 32-bit boundaries, are read with one 32-bit AHB access and are written with two separate non-sequential accesses.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:2ADDRR/W0x0Software writes here where the receive queue begins.

TBQBGMAC Transmit Buffer Queue Base Address Registerp. 496

offset 0x01C · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

  • Where the list of transmit buffer descriptors begins. Write it before NCR.TSTART starts transmission; once transmission has started, writes are ignored. The transmitter becomes active up to four MCK cycles after TSTART is written, and a write here within that time gives unpredictable results. A read gives the address of the descriptor now in use, which may not belong to the frame being sent, since the DMA handles two frames at a time. Descriptors sit on 32-bit boundaries, are written with one 32-bit AHB access and are read with two separate non-sequential accesses.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:2ADDRR/W0x0Software writes here where the transmit queue begins.

offset 0x030 · 32 bits · reset 0b00111111111111001111110011111111 · access R

  • Read-only view of the interrupt masks: a bit at 0 means that interrupt is enabled, 1 that it is not. Every bit is 1 after reset; a write of 1 to IER clears a bit and a write of 1 to IDR sets it. MANGMAC PHY Maintenance Registerp. 507

offset 0x034 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W · read/write

  • A write starts a shift that sends a PHY management frame on MDIO: each MDC cycle the top bit goes out on MDIO and the bottom bit is taken in from it. NSR.IDLE is set and an interrupt raised when it ends, about 2000 MCK cycles with MDC at MCK/32. A read during the shift returns the shift register as it stands; at the end the bits are back in place, with DATA holding the PHY's data after a read. The values written must form a valid management frame. Clause 22 and clause 45 PHYs are both served; WZO, CLTTO and OP are 0, 1, 10 for a clause 22 read; 0, 1, 01 for a clause 22 write; 0, 0, 11 for a clause 45 read; 0, 0, 01 for a clause 45 write; 0, 0, 10 for a clause 45 read with address.

17:16WTNR/W0x0Write as binary 10.
10Required.

15:0DATAR/W0x0For a write, the data to send to the PHY; after a read, the data the PHY returned.

STATUS.READY must be 1 when the command is issued. PSRProtocol Statusp. 1176

offset 0x44 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000707 · access R · read-only

  • After a CAN FD frame with BRS set reaches its data phase, the next error or good frame shows in DLEC, not LEC.
  • A bad fixed stuff bit in a CAN FD CRC sequence is reported as a form error, not a stuff error.
  • Setting or clearing CCCR.INIT does not shorten Bus_Off recovery. On Bus_Off the CAN sets CCCR.INIT itself and stops bus activity.
  • Once the CPU clears CCCR.INIT, the CAN waits for 129 bus idle periods of 11 recessive bits each, then resumes and resets its error counters.
  • During that wait each run of 11 recessive bits writes a Bit0 error code to PSR.LEC and is counted in ECR.REC, so the CPU can follow the recovery and tell whether the bus is stuck dominant or disturbed.

TXBRPTx Buffer Request Pendingp. 1215

offset 0xCC · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R · read-only

  • A TXBRP bit set during a Tx scan is left out of that scan; if that buffer is then cancelled, its add request is dropped at once and the TXBRP bit cleared.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:0TRPnone per bitR0x0One pending-request bit per Tx Buffer, set only for buffers TXBC configures. Setting one starts a Tx scan for the highest-priority request (lowest Message ID). A bit clears when its transmission completes or is cancelled through TXBCR; a cancel during a transmission takes effect when it ends, successful or not, and the TXBCR bit clears right after. A finished cancellation shows in TXBCF after a good transmission (with its TXBTO bit), when transmission had not started, on lost arbitration, or on a transmit error. With DAR set every unsuccessful transmission is cancelled and its TXBCF bit set.
0Nothing pending.
1Request pending.

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:0ARnone per bitR/W0x0One add-request bit per Tx Buffer: writing 1 sets it, 0 does nothing, so one write can queue several buffers. Set only for buffers TXBC configures. The bits clear at once if no Tx scan is running, otherwise when the scan ends.

SSARSDMA System Address / Argument 2 Registerp. 1241

offset 0x00 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
31:0ADDRR/W0x0In an SDMA transfer, the system memory address; after the SDMA transfer stops it holds the address of the next contiguous data, and writing the next address restarts the transfer. Access it only while no transaction runs; reads during a transfer can be invalid; an interrupt can ask software to update it. With Auto CMD23 it holds the 32-bit block count sent as the CMD23 argument: the full 32 bits with ADMA, limited by BCR (65535 blocks at most) without ADMA.

At 0 (4 Kbytes) the low 12 bits of SSAR address data inside the buffer and the upper 20 bits locate the buffer. Active only while TMR.DMAEN is 1.

BCRBlock Count Registerp. 1243

offset 0x06 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:0BLKCNTR/W0x0Number of blocks to transfer, 1 up to the maximum block count; used only when TMR.BCEN is 1 and only for multiple-block transfers. The peripheral counts it down after each block and stops at 0; at 0 no block is transferred. Access it only while no transaction runs: during a transfer reads can be invalid and writes are ignored. After a suspend command completes it reads the blocks still to transfer; the saved count is written back before a resume command.

TMRTransfer Mode Registerp. 1245

offset 0x0C · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

  • Set before sending a command that transfers data (CR.DPSEL) or a Resume command; saved on Suspend and restored before Resume. Not writable while a data transaction runs; writes are ignored while PSR.CMDINHD is 1.
  • Transfer type: MSBSEL 0, single transfer; MSBSEL 1 with BCEN 0, infinite transfer; MSBSEL 1, BCEN 1, BLKCNT non-zero, multiple transfer; MSBSEL 1, BCEN 1, BLKCNT 0, multiple transfer stopped.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
5MSBSELR/W0Write 1 for multiple-block transfer commands on the DAT lines and 0 for every other command. At 0, BCR need not be written.
4DTDSELR/W0Direction of DAT line data: 1 moves data from the card or device to the peripheral; 0 for all other commands.
0WRITEPeripheral to device (write).
1READDevice to peripheral (read).
3:2ACMDENR/W0x0Selects an automatic command for ending multiple-block reads and writes. At 1 (Auto CMD12) the peripheral sends CMD12 after the last block, only if the command needs it; errors go to ACESR. At 2 (Auto CMD23) the peripheral sends CMD23 before the command written to CR, with SSAR as its 32-bit block count argument, and skips the second command if the CMD23 response has errors (reported in ACESR). Auto CMD23 needs a card supporting CMD23 (SCR[33] = 1), ADMA rather than SDMA if DMA is used, and only CMD18 or CMD25; the command index is not checked.

1CMD12Auto CMD12.
2CMD23Auto CMD23.

1ENABLEBlock count on.
0DMAENR/W0Enables DMA, possible only when CA0R.ADMA2SUP shows it is supported; HC1R.DMASEL picks the DMA mode. Without DMA support it has no meaning and reads 0. When 1, a DMA operation starts on a write to the upper byte of CR.
0DISABLEDMA off.
1ENABLEDMA on.

24CMDLLR0Level of the CMD line, for error recovery and debugging.
23:20DATLLR0xFLevels of DAT[3:0], for error recovery and debugging, such as reading the busy level on DAT[0].

1Card present (CD = 0).

0Reset or debouncing.
1Stable: no card or card inserted.
16CARDINSR0Debounced card-present state. A 0-to-1 change sets NISTR.CINS when NISTER.CINS is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.CINS is 1); a 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.CREM when NISTER.CREM is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.CREM is 1). SRR.SWRSTALL does not affect it.
11BUFRDENR0For non-DMA reads: 1 while readable data is in the buffer. It falls when all block data has been read and rises when block data is ready, which sets NISTR.BRDRDY when NISTER.BRDRDY is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BRDRDY is 1).
10BUFWRENR0For non-DMA writes: 1 while the buffer has room for write data. It falls when all block data has been written and rises when the start of block data can be written, which sets NISTR.BWRRDY when NISTER.BWRRDY is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BWRRDY is 1).
9RTACTR01 while a read transfer is active. Set after the end bit of a read command, or when a read restarts through BGCR.CONTR. Cleared when the last block of BLKSIZE has gone to the system (for ADMA2, the descriptor table marks the end), or when all valid blocks are transferred and none is in progress after BGCR.STPBGR. A 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.TRFC when NISTER.TRFC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.TRFC is 1).
8WTACTR01 while a write transfer is active; 0 means no valid write data is held. Set after the end bit of a write command, or when a write restarts through BGCR.CONTR. Cleared after the CRC status of the last block of the transfer count (for ADMA2, from the descriptor table), or of a block where BGCR.STPBGR stops the transfer. During a write stopped by STPBGR, a 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.BLKGE when NISTER.BLKGE is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BLKGE is 1). Shows whether commands not using DAT can be sent during write busy.
3RTREQR0Set when the peripheral asks software to re-tune because temperature drift moved the data window and the tuned sampling point lost margin. Cleared when a command is sent by setting HC2R.EXTUN. A 0-to-1 change sets NISTR.RTEVT when NISTER.RTEVT is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.RTEVT is 1). Never set while HC2R.SCLKSEL is 0 (fixed sampling clock).
0Fixed or well-tuned sampling clock.
1Re-tuning needed.
2DLACTR01 while a DAT line is in use. Read: set after the read command's end bit or on BGCR.CONTR; cleared when the final block's end bit arrives (for ADMA2, the descriptor table's last transfer) or when a read stops at a block gap after BGCR.STPBGR, which sets NISTR.BLKGE when NISTER.BLKGE is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.BLKGE is 1). The read is held by driving Read Wait on DAT[2] or by stopping the SD clock; if Read Wait is already driven because the buffer is full, it stays driven to hold the read. Suspend/Resume needs Read Wait. Write: set after the write command's end bit or on BGCR.CONTR; cleared once the card ends its busy signal on the final block (no busy for 8 SDCLK counts as not busy; for ADMA2, the descriptor table's last transfer), or when the card ends busy ahead of a block-gap stop requested by BGCR.STPBGR. Command with busy: set after the command's end bit, cleared when busy ends. For writes and busy commands, a 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.TRFC when NISTER.TRFC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.TRFC is 1).
0DAT lines idle.
1DAT line in use.
1CMDINHDR01 when DLACT or RTACT is 1; 0 means the next command may be sent. Commands with busy (R1b, R5b) count here. A 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.TRFC when NISTER.TRFC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.TRFC is 1). After it falls, software can save registers 0x000 to 0x00D for a suspend.
0A command using DAT may be sent.
1No command using DAT may be sent.
0CMDINHCR00 when the CMD line is free and a command may be sent on it. Set as soon as CR is written; cleared when the response arrives. With Auto CMD12 or Auto CMD23 it is cleared by the read/write command's response, not by the CMD12 or CMD23 response. It does not show that Auto CMD12 is being sent, so a command written during Auto CMD12 is sent as well as CMD12. While it is 0, CMD-only commands may be sent even if CMDINHD is 1. A 1-to-0 change sets NISTR.CMDC when NISTER.CMDC is 1 (interrupt when NISIER.CMDC is 1). On a command conflict (EISTR.CMDCRC) or a Command Not Issued by Auto CMD12 error it stays 1 and CMDC is not set.
0A CMD-only command may be sent.
1No command may be sent.

2BLKGER/W0Set when a read or write stops at a block gap, only while BGCR.STPBGR is 1: for a read on the falling edge of PSR.DLACT (needs Read Wait), for a write on the falling edge of PSR.WTACT after the CRC status. Set only when NISTER.BLKGE is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.BLKGE is 1. Writing 1 clears it.
0No block gap event.
1Transaction stopped at a block gap.
1TRFCR/W0Set when a read or write transfer or a command with busy completes. Read: on the falling edge of PSR.RTACT, when the data length is done and read by the system, or when a stop at the block gap through BGCR.STPBGR finishes. Write: on the falling edge of PSR.DLACT, when the last data is written and busy released, or when a block-gap stop finishes with busy released. Command with busy: when busy ends. Set only when NISTER.TRFC is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.TRFC is 1. Writing 1 clears it. TRFC outranks EISTR.DATTEO: with both 1 the command has completed.
0Transfer not finished.
1Transfer finished.
0CMDCR/W0Set at the end bit of a command response; with Auto CMD12 or Auto CMD23, by the read/write command's response, not the CMD12 or CMD23 one. Set only when NISTER.CMDC is 1; interrupts only when NISIER.CMDC is 1. Writing 1 clears it. EISTR.CMDTEO outranks CMDC: CMDTEO 1 (CMDC either) means no response within 64 SDCLK cycles; CMDC 1 with CMDTEO 0 means a response was received; both 0, interrupted by another factor.
0No command completed.
1A command completed.

15PVALENR/W01 makes the peripheral set CCR.SDCLKFSEL, CCR.CLKGSEL and HC2R.DRVSEL from the PVR for automatic SDCLK frequency setting regardless of the system; 0 leaves CCR.CLKGSEL and CCR.SDCLKFSEL to the user.

Writing 1 is ignored; writing 0 resets the tuning circuit, and setting EXTUN also clears it. A reset tuning circuit takes time to tune again, so keeping it at 1 lets re-tuning finish quickly. Must not change while a response or read block is being received.

1Tuned sampling clock.

With PVALEN 1 it selects the PVR from which CCR.SDCLKFSEL, CCR.CLKGSEL and DRVSEL are loaded. Clear CCR.SDCLKEN before changing it to avoid a clock glitch, then set SDCLKEN again. Effective only while MC1R.DDR is 0.

A single conversion without averaging gives 12 bits: with CTRLB.LEFTADJ set, the high byte is in [15:8] and the other 4 bits in [7:4], so an 8-bit result can be read from the high byte alone; right-adjusted without oversampling, it is in [11:0].
